name: CT-RATE
description: CT-RATE is a public dataset that pairs 3D medical images with corresponding textual reports. It comprises 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients, with each scan accompanied by its corresponding radiology report. The dataset includes 50,188 reconstructed 3D chest CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices). Each volume is annotated with 18 abnormalities. CT-RATE is used to develop CT-CLIP, a CT-focused contrastive language-image pretraining framework, and CT-CHAT, a vision-language foundational chat model for 3D chest CT volumes.
creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Bjoern Menze, and colleagues from University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Istanbul Medipol University, Boston University, NIH, Imperial College London, ETH Zurich, University Hospital Zurich, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg
citeAs: Hamamci, I.E., Er, S., Wang, C., et al. Generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography.
rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE was curated from chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The dataset includes non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. CT volumes are reconstructed using various techniques to suit different window settings. The study received ethical approval from the Clinical Research Ethics Committee at Istanbul Medipol University (E-10840098-772.02-6841, 27/10/2023). All chest CT volumes, associated metadata, and radiology text reports were anonymized before computational analysis.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The RAD-ChestCT external validation set lacks a Mosaic attenuation label, which was excluded from external evaluation. The RAD-ChestCT dataset also lacks paired radiology reports, limiting report-to-volume retrieval evaluation to the internal validation set. Detailed metadata for the second external validation set (UPMC) is not publicly available as it is a private dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. CT volumes were acquired using Philips (61.5%), Siemens (30.1%), and PNMS (8.4%) CT scanners. Radiology reports are structured into four sections: clinical information, technique, findings, and impression. Reports were originally in Turkish and translated to English using the Google Translate API.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing all personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals using regular expressions to identify and eliminate date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. Anonymized reports were translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API, and bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations. For CT volumes, volumes involving contrast material or body parts other than the chest were excluded. Each chest CT volume's orientation was standardized by examining its metadata. All identifying information about patients and medical professionals was removed from the metadata.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each volume was resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. CT volumes were then either center-cropped or padded to reach a consistent resolution of 480 × 480 × 240. Each CT volume was converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from the metadata. HU values were clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000. During training, values were normalized to a range of -1 to 1.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-abnormality labels were extracted from radiology reports using an automated text classifier. This involved finetuning a pretrained language model, RadBERT (RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m), on 1,000 manually annotated reports for 18 distinct abnormalities. The annotated reports were divided into training (80%, 800 reports) and validation (20%, 200 reports) sets. Conditions not referenced in either the findings or impression section were considered absent. Similar conditions were grouped: left and right mucoid impactions under mucoid impaction; various lung opacities under lung opacity; lung and fissural nodules as lung nodules. The finetuned model was then applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned RadBERT model's precision, recall, and F1 scores were evaluated across 18 abnormalities, showing robust classification. F1 scores ranged from 0.95 to 1.00 across abnormalities. For the RAD-ChestCT external validation set, the higher classification probabilities between Arterial wall calcification and Coronary artery wall calcification labels were used for the Calcification prediction.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected report translations. Three board-certified radiologists (two thoracic radiologists from Zurich and one from Istanbul) independently rated reports for expert evaluation of CT-CHAT.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (finetuned for automated label extraction from radiology reports); Llama 3.1 7B/8B (for generating VQA question-answer pairs); TotalSegmentator (for organ-level anatomical segmentation labels); Google Translate API (for report translation from Turkish to English)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: CT-RATE is publicly accessible via https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibrahimhamamci/CT-RATE. The authors plan to extend CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels for 3D chest CT volumes as future work. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels are already openly available through the CT-RATE repository on Hugging Face.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient age (ranging from 18 to 102 years, mean 48.8 years), sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male). All personal information was anonymized before release, including removal of patient and medical professional identifiers from reports and metadata.
rai:dataSocialImpact: CT-RATE addresses critical challenges in 3D medical imaging AI by providing the first large-scale open-source dataset pairing 3D chest CT volumes with radiology reports. This enables development of foundation models that can assist radiologists, reduce workload, improve diagnostic accuracy, and potentially save lives in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available. The open-source release lays groundwork for future innovations in medical AI and improved patient care.
rai:dataBiases: CT-RATE is a single-institution dataset from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital in Türkiye, which may introduce biases that limit generalizability to other populations. The data originates from a single geographic and clinical setting. Performance increases with larger training sets, suggesting that incorporating data from multiple institutions and more diverse patient populations could further enhance model robustness. CT-CLIP depends on the specific terminology used in reports, and variability in how diseases are described across radiology reports can affect detection accuracy.
rai:dataLimitations: CT-RATE is a single-center dataset, which may limit generalizability to other populations and geographic regions. Current models are limited to chest CT volumes and do not cover other 3D imaging modalities (MRI, PET) or other anatomical regions. CT-CLIP depends on specific terminology in reports and prompt engineering choices. The absence of true 3D benchmarks for multimodal AI assistants limits comparison. Report generation quality remains insufficient for clinical deployment. The dataset does not yet include multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels (planned for future work).
rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of AI models for: (1) multi-abnormality detection in 3D chest CT volumes, (2) contrastive language-image pretraining (CT-CLIP), (3) visual question answering for 3D chest CT (CT-CHAT), (4) radiology report generation, (5) volume-to-volume and report-to-volume retrieval, (6) zero-shot classification of chest CT abnormalities. The dataset includes a VQA dataset of over 2.7 million question-answer pairs derived from CT-RATE for fine-tuning vision-language models.
